Explain, in three short paragraphs, why.text:
During the day, sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere and collides with gas molecules that are much smaller than the wavelength of visible light. This causes a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which shorter wavelengths—blue and violet—are scattered far more efficiently than longer ones. Although violet light scatters even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue, and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so the sky appears blue.

At sunset, sunlight must travel through a much longer path of atmosphere because the Sun is low on the horizon. Over that greater distance, most of the blue and green light is scattered away before it reaches our eyes
